sections.h2: Which Jesup office sends the Wayne County tax bill?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner's office on East Walnut Street sends it, and the assessors beside it decide the value. Walk in at 341 E Walnut St, Jesup, GA 31546, mail PO Box 287 (ZIP 31598), or phone (912) 427-5910 between 8:30am and 5:00pm.

A single bill gathers money for five bodies. The commissioner's site names the State, the City of Odum, the City of Screven, the county and the school board. The Wayne County Board of Commissioners, Board of Education and the two cities set their own millage, while the Chief Appraiser and Board of Assessors supply the values. Whoever owns the parcel on January 1 is the person billed.

Reach the assessor at (912) 427-5920 about value, and the commissioner about payment, penalties or a payoff. The same counter registers vehicles for the state and collects the title fee, so lines can be busy near tag deadlines.

sections.h2: What shapes the Wayne County market for sellers?
sections.html:
Wayne is a big, thinly settled county on the Altamaha River with growth that has outpaced most of its neighbors. QuickFacts has 32,481 residents for July 2025, up from 30,141 in the April 2020 base, a gain of 7.8%, across 641.81 square miles of land. The county's own web page says the river marks the northeast boundary and runs along more than 60 miles of frontage.

Lake Lindsay Grace is the other landmark the county promotes. It lies about 4.5 miles south of Highway 84 along Highway 203 and holds roughly 240 acres of water, with two parks and three boat launches. Odum and Screven are the incorporated towns besides Jesup.

  • Density: 47.0 residents per square mile in 2020.
  • Homes: 13,180 units, two-thirds lived in by owners.
  • Midpoint home value among owners in the 2020 through 2024 survey: $162,800.
  • Midpoint rent: $846, with 102 construction permits in 2025.
  • Households: 11,061, and median household income of $53,427.

Jobs rose 11.1% between 2022 and 2023 to 7,669 across 639 employer businesses, with a payroll near $345.8 million. Health care and social assistance brought in $178.6 million in 2022, and retail sales were $423.3 million. A buyer commuting from the county to jobs elsewhere faces a mean drive of 28.0 minutes.

sections.h2: Wayne County due dates and what happens after them
sections.html:
Real estate and business personal property tax is normally due on November 15, after bills go out around September 15. Mobile home tax falls due on April 1, and a missed deadline adds a 10% penalty. Vehicle tax is tied to the owner's birthday.

Interest starts the day after the due date at a rate reset each January, and 120 days later the first of four penalty steps lands at 5%. Every further 120 days brings another step until the penalty hits 20%. The commissioner cites state code sections 48-2-40 and 48-2-44 for those rules.

Ask for a payoff dated to your closing day, since interest keeps adding. The commissioner warns that property with unpaid tax may be levied upon and ultimately sold, and a mobile home owner who wants a different value files a return with the assessors between January 1 and March 15.

sections.h2: How does a Wayne County owner contest a value?
sections.html:
Mail the appeal inside 45 days of the date the assessment notice went out, to Board of Tax Assessors, PO Box 174, Jesup, GA 31598. The notice lists the new value, the old one, the reason for the change and estimated tax at the estimated rollback millage. Complaints about the size of the bill are not grounds, because the appeal is about value.

The board takes a second look and tells you what it decided. If you remain unhappy the file moves to the county Board of Equalization for a hearing, and a further appeal can reach Superior Court. Arbitration is offered instead of the equalization hearing, and the assessors can explain how it works.

Property is assessed at 40% of market value. You can also file a return between January 1 and April 1 stating a value of your own, which starts the appeal process if the board turns your number down. Returns on real property renew automatically at last year's value until something about the property changes.

sections.h2: Wayne County homestead exemption: who qualifies and when to file
sections.html:
Wayne has local exemptions, and the local amount replaces the state one whenever it is larger. You qualify by owning and living in the house on January 1, and the application goes to the assessors. Once approved it renews itself until you move, sell or change categories.

The commissioner's FAQ says the filing cutoff is April 1, while the property page names March 1. Ask the assessor which date counts for this year before you rely on the exemption. A late form takes effect the next tax year.

Standing timber follows its own rule. It escapes tax until it is sold or harvested, and then it is taxed on its full market value at the millage rate.

sections.h2: What should a Wayne County seller do about the bill at closing?
sections.html:
Treat the bill as a line on the closing statement and collect a written balance first. A house that sells in October still produces a full-year bill in the January 1 owner's name, so the closing attorney divides it between buyer and seller. The payoff figure tells the title company how much to remit.

  • Ask for balances on every open year, with penalty and interest.
  • Check whether the lot lies in Odum or Screven and picks up a city bill.
  • Confirm homestead status so the buyer knows whether to apply.
  • Order a copy of your deed from the Clerk of Superior Court if the title company wants one.
  • Find out whether a mobile home on the lot is billed separately.

The county's directory lists helpful numbers for a seller sorting out paperwork: Probate Court at 912-427-5940, Veterans Affairs at 912-427-5909, and Legal Aid at 800-255-0056 for Brunswick and 800-498-9508 for Waycross.

faqs.q: What number reaches the Wayne County Tax Commissioner?
faqs.a: Call (912) 427-5910. The office is at 341 E Walnut St in Jesup and keeps hours from 8:30am to 5:00pm. For value questions, call the assessor at (912) 427-5920.

faqs.q: When does Wayne County expect real estate tax?
faqs.a: Payment is normally due on November 15, with bills mailed by September 15. Mobile homes follow a separate April 1 date.

faqs.q: How many days does a Wayne County owner have to appeal?
faqs.a: Forty-five days, counted from the date the assessment notice was mailed. Send the appeal to PO Box 174, Jesup, GA 31598. It has to challenge value, because the size of the bill is not appealable.

faqs.q: What does Wayne County charge on late tax?
faqs.a: Interest begins the day after the due date, and a 5% penalty arrives 120 days later. The penalty keeps stepping up every 120 days to 20%, and the interest rate resets each January.

faqs.q: What fraction of market value is taxable in Wayne County?
faqs.a: Forty percent. Exemptions are subtracted from that assessed figure, and the millage rate applies to what is left.
